title: 10. Resource Cleanup Guide
content:
In this step, we’ll systematically clean up all AWS resources created during the workshop to avoid ongoing charges.
Critical: Follow the cleanup steps in the exact order shown below. Deleting resources out of order may cause dependency errors.
Step 1: Disable CloudFront Distribution Open the CloudFront Console Select your distribution Click Edit → Change Distribution state to Disabled Click Save changes Distribution disabling takes 15-20 minutes. You cannot delete a distribution until it’s fully disabled.
Step 2: Delete Application Load Balancer Open the EC2 Console → Load Balancers Select your load balancer → Actions → Delete Confirm deletion by typing the load balancer name Navigate to Target Groups → Select target group → Delete Step 3: Terminate EC2 Instances Go to EC2 Console → Instances Select your caching-app-server instance Instance state → Terminate instance Confirm termination Repeat for any test instances created during the workshop Step 4: Delete ElastiCache Redis Cluster Open ElastiCache Console → Redis OSS caches Select your product-cache cluster Actions → Delete Configure deletion options: Create final backup: No Type cluster name: product-cache Click Delete Navigate to Subnet groups → Delete redis-subnet-group Redis cluster deletion takes 5-10 minutes.
Step 5: Delete DAX Cluster Open DynamoDB Console → DAX → Clusters Select your product-dax-cluster Actions → Delete Confirm deletion by typing the cluster name Navigate to Subnet groups → Delete dax-subnet-group DAX cluster deletion takes 10-15 minutes.
Step 6: Delete DynamoDB Table In DynamoDB Console → Tables Select the ProductCatalog table Actions → Delete table Configure deletion options: Create backup before deleting: Unchecked Type table name: ProductCatalog Click Delete table Step 7: Delete CloudFront Distribution Return to CloudFront Console Verify your distribution shows “Disabled” status Select the distribution → Delete Confirm deletion Step 8: Delete IAM Roles Open IAM Console → Roles Search for and delete these roles: CachingAppRole DAXServiceRole For each role: Select → Delete → Type role name to confirm Step 9: Delete VPC and Networking Resources Open VPC Console → Security Groups Delete custom security groups in this order: app-sg redis-sg dax-sg alb-sg You cannot delete the default security group. Only delete the custom ones you created.
Go to Your VPCs Select your caching-workshop-vpc Actions → Delete VPC Confirm deletion by typing “delete” Deleting the VPC will automatically delete associated subnets, route tables, internet gateway, and NAT gateways.
Step 10: Clean Up CloudWatch Resources CloudWatch Console → Dashboards
Delete MultiLayerCachingDashboard Alarms → All alarms
Select all workshop-related alarms → Delete Log groups
Delete /aws/ec2/caching-app log group Step 11: Delete SNS Topics Open SNS Console → Topics Select the caching-alerts topic Delete → Type “delete me” to confirm Step 12: Verify Complete Cleanup Check each service to ensure all resources are deleted:
✅ Verification Checklist EC2 Console:
Instances: Terminated Load Balancers: Deleted Target Groups: Deleted VPC Console:
VPC: Deleted Security Groups: Only default remaining Subnets: Deleted NAT Gateways: Deleted ElastiCache Console:
Redis Clusters: Deleted Subnet Groups: Deleted DynamoDB Console:
Tables: Deleted DAX Clusters: Deleted DAX Subnet Groups: Deleted CloudFront Console:
Distributions: Deleted CloudWatch Console:
Dashboards: Deleted Alarms: Deleted Log Groups: Deleted SNS Console:
Topics: Deleted IAM Console:
Custom Roles: Deleted Step 13: Check Billing Dashboard Go to Billing Dashboard Verify no ongoing charges for workshop resources It may take up to 24 hours for all charges to stop appearing in your billing dashboard after resource deletion.
Troubleshooting Common Issues Cannot Delete VPC Cause: Resources still depend on the VPC Solution: Check for remaining ENIs, verify all instances terminated
Cannot Delete Security Group Cause: Security group still referenced by other resources Solution: Ensure all instances and load balancers are deleted first
CloudFront Distribution Won’t Delete Cause: Distribution not fully disabled Solution: Wait for “Disabled” status (up to 20 minutes)
DAX Cluster Deletion Fails Cause: Cluster still being accessed Solution: Stop all applications, wait a few minutes, try again
